Write a polynomial-time reduction from 3-SAT to Independent Set. problems.py defines both problems: SOURCE is 3-SAT and TARGET is Independent Set. The SOURCE and TARGET class docstrings give the exact instance formats, yes-conditions and edge cases.

PROBLEM DEFINITIONS (the SOURCE and TARGET docstrings from problems.py, complete as given here):

SOURCE = ThreeSat
3-SAT.

Instance: {"num_vars": m, "clauses": [[l1, l2, l3], ...]}
  * Variables are 1..m. A literal is +v (v is true) or -v (v is false).
  * Every clause has exactly 3 literals on 3 different variables, so a
    clause may not repeat a variable or contain both v and -v.
  * Literal order inside a clause and clause order do not matter. The
    same clause may appear more than once.
  * Variables need not all appear in a clause.

Yes iff some assignment of true/false to variables 1..m makes every
clause contain at least one true literal.

Edge cases: a formula with no clauses is satisfiable (yes), for any m,
including m = 0. A formula with clauses needs m >= 3.

TARGET = IndependentSet
Independent Set.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has an independent set of AT LEAST k vertices: k
vertices with no edge between any two of them.

Edge cases: k <= 0 is always yes. k > n is always no. With no edges,
every set of vertices is independent.

function.arguments:
{"command":"cd /tmp/reduction-_4bnz3vi && cat <<'EOF' > reduce.py
"""Polynomial-time reduction from 3-SAT (SOURCE) to Independent Set (TARGET).

Construction (standard clause-triangle reduction):

  * For every clause c_i = (l1, l2, l3) create three vertices
    (3*i, 3*i+1, 3*i+2), one per literal occurrence.
  * Add the three edges of a triangle among those three vertices, so an
    independent set can pick at most one literal from each clause.
  * For every pair of vertices in *different* clauses whose literals are
    contradictory (x and -x), add an edge, so an independent set may not
    pick both.
  * Set k = number of clauses.

A set of k vertices with no internal edge must pick exactly one vertex from
each of the k clause triangles; the cross edges force the chosen literals to
be simultaneously satisfiable, and any satisfying assignment yields such a
set.  Hence the graph has an independent set of size >= k iff the formula is
satisfiable.

Edge cases:
  * No clauses: n = 0, edges = [], k = 0.  k <= 0 is always yes, matching
    the empty (satisfiable) formula.
  * Repeated clauses simply get their own triangles; the argument is
    unchanged because each triangle still contributes at most one vertex.

The construction uses O(#clauses) vertices and O(#clauses^2) edges, so it
runs in polynomial time and never calls a brute-force solver.
"""


def reduce(instance):
    """Reduce a 3-SAT instance to an Independent Set instance."""
    clauses = instance["clauses"]

    n = 3 * len(clauses)
    edges = []
    seen = set()

    def add_edge(u, v):
        if u == v:
            return
        key = (u, v) if u < v else (v, u)
        if key not in seen:
            seen.add(key)
            edges.append([u, v])

    # Triangle for each clause: at most one literal per clause may be chosen.
    for i in range(len(clauses)):
        base = 3 * i
        add_edge(base, base + 1)
        add_edge(base + 1, base + 2)
        add_edge(base, base + 2)

    # Map each literal value to the vertices that represent it.
    literal_vertices = {}
    for i, clause in enumerate(clauses):
        for j, literal in enumerate(clause):
            literal_vertices.setdefault(literal, []).append(3 * i + j)

    # Edge between every pair of contradictory literals in different clauses.
    for literal, vertices in literal_vertices.items():
        for other in literal_vertices.get(-literal, ()):
            for u in vertices:
                for v in other:
                    add_edge(u, v)

    return {"n": n, "edges": edges, "k": len(clauses)}
EOF
echo "written" && ls -la reduce.py"}

"""Polynomial-time reduction from 3-SAT (SOURCE) to Independent Set (TARGET).

Construction (standard clause-triangle reduction):

  * For every clause c_i = (l1, l2, l3) create three vertices
    (3*i, 3*i+1, 3*i+2), one per literal occurrence.
  * Add the three edges of a triangle among those three vertices, so an
    independent set can pick at most one literal from each clause.
  * For every pair of vertices in *different* clauses whose literals are
    contradictory (x and -x), add an edge, so an independent set may not
    pick both.
  * Set k = number of clauses.

A set of k vertices with no internal edge must pick exactly one vertex from
each of the k clause triangles; the cross edges force the chosen literals to
be simultaneously satisfiable, and any satisfying assignment yields such a
set.  Hence the graph has an independent set of size >= k iff the formula is
satisfiable.

Edge cases:
  * No clauses: n = 0, edges = [], k = 0.  k <= 0 is always yes, matching
    the empty (satisfiable) formula.
  * Repeated clauses simply get their own triangles; the argument is
    unchanged because each triangle still contributes at most one vertex.

The construction uses O(#clauses) vertices and O(#clauses^2) edges, so it
runs in polynomial time and never calls a brute-force solver.
"""


def reduce(instance):
    """Reduce a 3-SAT instance to an Independent Set instance."""
    clauses = instance["clauses"]

    n = 3 * len(clauses)
    edges = []
    seen = set()

    def add_edge(u, v):
        if u == v:
            return
        key = (u, v) if u < v else (v, u)
        if key not in seen:
            seen.add(key)
            edges.append([u, v])

    # Triangle for each clause: at most one literal per clause may be chosen.
    for i in range(len(clauses)):
        base = 3 * i
        add_edge(base, base + 1)
        add_edge(base + 1, base + 2)
        add_edge(base, base + 2)

    # Map each literal value to the vertices that represent it.
    literal_vertices = {}
    for i, clause in enumerate(clauses):
        for j, literal in enumerate(clause):
            literal_vertices.setdefault(literal, []).append(3 * i + j)

    # Edge between every pair of contradictory literals in different clauses.
    for literal, vertices in literal_vertices.items():
        for other in literal_vertices.get(-literal, ()):
            for u in vertices:
                for v in other:
                    add_edge(u, v)

    return {"n": n, "edges": edges, "k": len(clauses)}
